meta.pack_name: EU Cyber Resilience Act Readiness Programme
meta.classification_label: Illustrative engagement — fictional client data; regulatory facts verified to 30 Oct 2026

brand.voice: Calm, exact, decision-oriented. British English. Action titles that state the so-what. No hype, no emoji.

fonts.fallbacks: Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif / system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Arial, sans-serif

rules: Every slide/page has an action title: one full sentence stating the so-what (max ~15 words).
One message per slide; a tracker/section label top-left; source line bottom-left on any data slide.
Client numbers carry an 'Illustrative' tag; vendor/survey numbers carry their source and type.
Money as EUR with 'm'/'k' (EUR 9.3m, EUR 210k) or the euro sign; dates as 11 Dec 2027.
RAG colours only for status; accent teal for emphasis; signal orange only for the binding constraint.
No real company names for the client, no named individuals: roles only.

storyline.governing_thought: The CRA turns product cybersecurity into a licence to sell in the EU. Example Group can be ready by 11 Dec 2027, but only if it secures third-party assessment capacity and builds shared compliance infrastructure in the next two quarters.

scqa.situation: The Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847) has been in force since 10 Dec 2024. Article 14 reporting has applied since 11 Sep 2026 to every in-scope product, including those already sold. Everything else applies from 11 Dec 2027.
scqa.complication: Three things make this harder than a normal compliance project: reporting is already live on a 24-hour clock; seven of Example Group's thirteen product families need a notified body or a cited harmonised standard, and neither exists today; and compliance must be proven with evidence for every product version for at least ten years.
scqa.question: What must Example Group do, by when and at what cost to keep selling in the EU after 11 Dec 2027?
scqa.answer: Run a 14-month, three-wave programme (Project Rampart): build shared capabilities once (PSIRT, SBOM, secure updates, evidence system), apply them product by product, and lock in notified-body capacity by Q1 2027. Investment is about EUR 9.3m to Dec 2027 and EUR 1.8m a year to run. The board is asked to take five decisions on 19 Nov 2026.

pillars.title: Reporting is already law
pillars.message: Every in-scope product — legacy included — is on a 24-hour reporting clock today.
pillars.proof: Art 14 applies since 11 Sep 2026 (Art 69(3)); early warning 24h, notification 72h, final report 14 days / 1 month.

pillars.title: Market access is the binding constraint
pillars.message: EUR 468m of annual EU revenue sits in Class I and II products that need a notified body that does not yet exist.
pillars.proof: No harmonised standard cited; no CRA notified body designated at checks to 8 Sep 2026; vendor estimates of 12-18 months per body.

pillars.title: Compliance is an evidence system, not a project
pillars.message: Build once, apply per product version, sustain for ten years.
pillars.proof: Annex VII file per version; retention 10 years or support period (Art 13(13)); PLD disclosure from 9 Dec 2026.

exposure.note: Fines are the higher of the fixed amount and the percentage of worldwide annual turnover. Enforcement machinery applies from 11 Dec 2027; micro and small enterprises are exempt from fines for missing the 24-hour deadlines (Art 64(10)(a)).

market_access.note: Products that cannot be assessed may not be placed on the EU market from 11 Dec 2027; authorities can order withdrawal or recall (Arts 54-58).

exposure.product_liability: Directive (EU) 2024/2853 applies to products placed on the market from 9 Dec 2026: software is a product, a vulnerability can be a defect, non-compliance with mandatory safety requirements raises a presumption of defectiveness (Art 10(2)(b)), and courts can order disclosure of evidence (Art 9).

legacy_decision.recommendation: Withdraw IR-300 and IS-200 from EU sale before 11 Dec 2027 and migrate customers to IR-500/IS-300; remediation would cost about EUR 1.4m plus notified-body fees for EUR 18m of declining EU revenue.

diagnostic.name: CRA Readiness Diagnostic

scale.name: Initial
scale.descriptor: Ad hoc or individual effort; not documented.

scale.name: Defined
scale.descriptor: Documented and partly applied; gaps known.

scale.name: Implemented
scale.descriptor: Applied consistently for this product, with evidence.

diagnostic.readiness_index_definition: Mean over questions of min(score, 3) / 3. Level 4 does not offset gaps elsewhere. 100% means every question at level 3 or above.

questions.text: A named executive is accountable for CRA compliance, with written authority to block a release and to sign EU declarations of conformity.
questions.evidence: Board or ExCo instrument naming the accountable executive and the DoC signatory
questions.action: Execute a signing instrument naming the DoC signatory, alternate and scope; write release-blocking authority into the sponsor's mandate.

questions.text: The core CRA roles (compliance lead, product security officer, PSIRT lead) are filled by named people with deputies.
questions.action: Appoint named role holders and deputies; publish the RACI with one accountable person per decision.

questions.text: A written product-risk acceptance rule excludes cost, risk appetite and commercial strategy as reasons to leave risk unaddressed.
questions.basis: Annex I Part I(1); guidance C(2026) 5252 paras 156-163
questions.evidence: Risk policy section for the product-risk category; acceptance log
questions.action: Add a product-risk category to the enterprise risk framework with its own acceptance authority and a non-cost appeal route.

questions.text: A programme board reviews CRA readiness monthly against KPIs drawn from a system of record.
questions.basis: Good practice; Annex VIII Module H pt 3.2
questions.action: Run a monthly programme board with a standing agenda and KPIs read from the system of record.

questions.text: Every product, version, variant, companion app and backend is in a register with a recorded scope decision.
questions.action: Build the register from release, commercial and cloud systems, then record a dated scope decision per row.

questions.text: Remote data processing boundaries are mapped per product function using the three-element test.
questions.action: Map every remote function to its service, developer and fallback; classify each as RDPS, component or out of scope.

questions.text: Each product has a documented class (default, Class I, Class II or critical) with a core-functionality rationale.
questions.evidence: Classification decision record citing the technical description
questions.action: Classify on core functionality against the Implementing Regulation's technical descriptions; take legal review on borderline cases.

questions.text: The economic-operator role per market and the legacy status of each product line are recorded.
questions.evidence: Role-per-market table; legacy flags in the register
questions.action: Record manufacturer, importer, distributor or representative per market; flag lines still sold after 11 Dec 2027.

domains.name: Risk assessment and secure by design

questions.text: A documented cybersecurity risk assessment exists for the product or family, covering intended purpose, foreseeable use and expected time in use.
questions.action: Run a TR-03183-1-style assessment on the representative product and sign it off through the second line.

questions.text: The assessment states whether and how each Annex I Part I(2)(a)-(m) item applies, with a justification for every item marked not applicable.
questions.action: Complete the 13-row applicability matrix; no row may be signed with a blank justification.

questions.text: Threat models and data-flow diagrams are maintained and updated on defined triggers, not on a calendar.
questions.basis: Art 13(3); Annex I Part II(3); guidance paras 238-240
questions.evidence: Threat model versions with change log
questions.action: Wire update triggers (security-relevant release, new vulnerability, new threat) into the release and PSIRT processes.

questions.text: Secure-by-default configuration (no default credentials, minimal exposed services, reset to original state) is verified at every release.
questions.action: Add a secure-default configuration check and a reset test to the release gate.

questions.text: A documented secure development lifecycle with a release security gate applies to every release.
questions.basis: Annex I Part I(1); Annex VIII Module H pt 3.2
questions.action: Define the release security gate and make its signed record a precondition for tagging a release.

questions.text: Every release is checked for known exploitable vulnerabilities against EUVD, NVD and the CISA KEV catalogue before it ships.
questions.basis: Annex I Part I(2)(a); guidance paras 230-237
questions.evidence: Scan reports and VEX tied to the release SBOM
questions.action: Automate a known-exploitable check that blocks the release unless each finding is fixed or carries a VEX justification.

questions.text: Security testing (static analysis, fuzzing, dynamic testing, penetration tests) is risk-driven and evidenced per release.
questions.basis: Annex I Part II(3); Annex VII point 6
questions.evidence: Test plan with review log; test reports
questions.action: Write a threat-driven test plan per product and keep a dated review log showing what was re-tested and why.

questions.text: Each release records a substantial-modification decision using the four-question test.
questions.evidence: Security-delta assessment on the gate record
questions.action: Add the four guidance questions to the release gate and route positive answers to a new declaration.

domains.name: Supply chain, SBOM and open source

questions.text: A machine-readable SBOM (CycloneDX 1.6+ or SPDX 3.0.1+) is generated from the shipped artefact for every release.
questions.basis: Annex I Part II(1); Annex VII point 2(b); BSI TR-03183-2
questions.evidence: Signed SBOM per release with quality score
questions.action: Generate SBOMs at build from the artefact, enrich to TR-03183-2 fields, sign and store them with the release.

questions.text: Third-party and open-source components pass a documented due-diligence gate before use.
questions.action: Run an intake gate on every new dependency recording need, maintenance signals, licence, vulnerability history and exit plan.

questions.text: Supplier contracts require vulnerability notification, SBOM delivery and support-period commitments.
questions.action: Add the CRA clause pack to master agreements, starting with suppliers of security-relevant components.

questions.text: Vulnerabilities found in components are reported upstream and fixes are shared with maintainers.
questions.evidence: Upstream report log in PSIRT case files
questions.action: Give PSIRT or the OSPO ownership of upstream reporting, with a duplicate check and legal pre-clearance for fix sharing.

questions.text: A coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy, a security.txt file and a non-automated contact channel are published.
questions.evidence: Published CVD policy URL; security.txt; intake monitoring log
questions.action: Publish the CVD policy and security.txt, add an anonymous web form and a monitored human channel.

questions.text: A PSIRT triages every report and monitoring hit for severity, reachability and active exploitation.
questions.evidence: PSIRT procedure; case files with UTC timestamps
questions.action: Open a case for every report and hit; record reachability and the exploitation decision in UTC.

questions.text: Fixed vulnerabilities are disclosed in public advisories, machine-readable where appropriate, with VEX for non-affected findings.
questions.basis: Annex I Part II(4); BSI TR-03183-3
questions.evidence: Advisory index; CSAF documents; VEX files
questions.action: Stand up an advisory page and a CSAF provider; publish VEX statements for findings that do not affect the product.

questions.text: Vulnerability case records are retained and response metrics are reported.
questions.action: Report acknowledgement and fix times quarterly and retain case files for 10 years or the support period.

questions.text: Updates are signed, verified before install, protected against rollback and recoverable after a failed install.
questions.basis: Annex I Part I(2)(c), (f); Annex I Part II(7)
questions.action: Move signing keys into an HSM, add anti-rollback counters and atomic install with recovery.

questions.text: Security updates install automatically by default where applicable, with user notification and a clear opt-out.
questions.evidence: Default configuration export; Annex II point 8(e) text
questions.action: Turn automatic security updates on by default, or record the Recital 56 carve-out in the risk assessment.

questions.text: Security fixes can ship separately from feature releases and remain available for at least 10 years.
questions.evidence: Maintenance branch policy; update repository retention
questions.action: Run security-only maintenance branches and an immutable update repository retained for 10 years.

questions.text: A support period is set per product from expected time in use, and the end date is shown at purchase.
questions.action: Determine the support period from expected use time (five years is a floor) and publish the end month and year.

questions.text: At least two Assigned Representatives are registered on the ENISA Single Reporting Platform with MFA, and the coordinator CSIRT is decided.
questions.evidence: SRP roster; coordinator CSIRT decision record
questions.action: Register two or more personal EU Logins with MFA and record the main-establishment decision before any incident.

questions.text: Written awareness criteria and a 24/7 on-call chain allow an early warning to be filed within 24 hours, including at weekends.
questions.evidence: PSIRT runbook; on-call rota; deputy chain
questions.action: Write the awareness test into the runbook and give the PSIRT lead and deputies authority to file without prior approval.

questions.text: Templates for the 24-hour, 72-hour and final reports and for user notification exist and have been rehearsed.
questions.action: Draft templates on the SRP glossary fields and run two paper drills a year, one vulnerability and one incident.

questions.text: Legacy and end-of-support products are included in the reportable inventory.
questions.action: Add every in-scope product still in use to the reportable inventory, including lines no longer sold or supported.

questions.text: An Annex VII technical file exists for each product version and is versioned with releases.
questions.action: Adopt the 13-part file outline and generate version-linked contents from the release pipeline.

questions.text: Annex II user information, including the support end date and the vulnerability contact, is drafted and ready to publish.
questions.action: Draft the Annex II document per product family and publish it at a stable, versioned URL.

questions.text: The EU declaration of conformity format, signing authority and CE marking placement are decided.
questions.evidence: DoC template; signing instrument; CE placement record
questions.action: Agree the DoC template and languages, the signing instrument and where the CE marking sits for hardware and software.

questions.text: Evidence sits in a system of record with 10-year retention and can answer a reasoned request within 10 working days.
questions.evidence: System of record; tested request export
questions.action: Select a system of record, compute retention per version and test an end-to-end reasoned-request export.

questions.text: The conformity route for the product (Module A, B+C or H) is decided, with a fallback.
questions.action: Decide the route per family; for Class I, plan third-party assessment until a harmonised standard is cited.

questions.text: Candidate notified bodies are shortlisted and a pre-assessment is contracted where the route needs one.
questions.action: Shortlist three candidates, contract pre-assessments with conversion options, and check NANDO at every programme board.

questions.text: A complete Module A internal-control record is kept for the product, even where a notified body will be used.
questions.action: Build the Module A record and evidence index now; it is the fallback and the body's application pack.

questions.text: EU representation, importer and distributor duties and marketplace arrangements are settled for each market.
questions.action: Confirm the role per market, appoint an authorised representative where useful and brief importers on their checks.

risks.title: No notified-body capacity in time
risks.description: No CRA notified body is designated with capacity before Q2 2027, so Class I/II families cannot be certified by 11 Dec 2027.
risks.mitigations: Pre-contract three candidates with conversion options; Module H for IC to cover five families with one body; check NANDO at every programme board; prioritise top-revenue SKUs.

risks.title: Engineering capacity
risks.description: Remediation competes with the 2027 product roadmap for the same engineers.
risks.mitigations: Ring-fence 26 FTE-years in the 2027 plan; defer two roadmap features; contractors for documentation and testing.

risks.title: No harmonised standard cited for Class I
risks.description: EN 304 6xx verticals are not cited in time, so Class I products cannot use Module A.
risks.mitigations: Plan Class I on third-party routes; align files to draft clause structure; switch to Module A only if a citation lands before assessment.

risks.title: SBOM and supplier transparency gaps
risks.description: Binary blobs and supplier components without SBOMs or vulnerability notification undermine Annex I Part II(1) and the 24-hour determination.
risks.mitigations: Binary SCA on firmware images; clause pack to top 15 suppliers first; exit plans for refusers.

risks.title: Legacy lines still sold after 11 Dec 2027
risks.description: IR-300 and IS-200 units placed after 11 Dec 2027 must comply with Annex I.
risks.mitigations: Board decision on 19 Nov 2026 to withdraw from EU sale and migrate customers; remediate only if the decision changes.

risks.title: Late or wrong Art 14 filing
risks.description: Awareness misjudged or a stale distribution map delays the 24-hour early warning.
risks.mitigations: Written awareness criteria; deputies with authority to file; distribution map refresh (T10); two drills a year.

risks.title: Scope undercount
risks.description: Versions, companion apps and backends found late enlarge the portfolio.
risks.mitigations: Build the register from release and cloud systems; second reconciliation after the first gate run.

risks.title: Key-person dependency in PSIRT
risks.description: Two people hold most PSIRT knowledge; on-call cannot be sustained.
risks.mitigations: Hire PSIRT lead; second analyst; documented runbook; cross-training from IC.

risks.title: Guidance changes
risks.description: Formal adoption of C(2026) 5252 or later FAQ versions change scope or support-period decisions.
risks.mitigations: Decision records cite the guidance version; quarterly standards and guidance review.

risks.title: Product-liability disclosure
risks.description: From 9 Dec 2026 claimants can seek disclosure of technical files and update logs under the PLD.
risks.mitigations: Write records for disclosure; legal review of risk acceptances; align with product liability insurance.

facts.statement: The CRA is Regulation (EU) 2024/2847; it entered into force on 10 Dec 2024.
Article 14 reporting applies from 11 Sep 2026 to all in-scope products, including those placed on the market before 11 Dec 2027.
Chapter IV (notification of conformity assessment bodies) applies from 11 Jun 2026; all other provisions from 11 Dec 2027.

Reporting clocks: actively exploited vulnerability 24h early warning, 72h notification, final report 14 days after a corrective measure is available; severe incident 24h, 72h, final report 1 month after the 72h notification.
Reports go through ENISA's Single Reporting Platform to the coordinator CSIRT of the main-establishment Member State; the platform has been live since 11 Sep 2026 (web form, English only, no API).
Fines: up to EUR 15m or 2.5% of worldwide annual turnover (Annex I, Arts 13-14); EUR 10m or 2% (other obligations); EUR 5m or 1% (misleading information), whichever is higher.
No harmonised standard is cited in the OJ and no common specification is adopted (30 Oct 2026); Class I products cannot use Module A until one is cited and applied in full.
No CRA notified body was verifiably designated in NANDO at checks to 8 Sep 2026; Member States must 'strive' for enough bodies by 11 Dec 2026.
Annexes III and IV list 19 Class I, 4 Class II and 3 critical categories (26 in total); Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2392 gives their technical descriptions (in force 21 Dec 2025).
Commission guidance C(2026) 5252 (content approved 27 Jul 2026) is non-binding and formally pending adoption in all languages; FAQ v1.4 is dated 4 Sep 2026.

Support period must reflect expected time in use and be at least five years unless the product is expected to be used for less; security updates stay available for at least 10 years or the rest of the support period.
Technical documentation and the declaration are kept for 10 years after placing on the market or the support period, whichever is longer.
The SBOM is part of the technical documentation; manufacturers are not obliged to make it public.
facts.basis: Annex I Part II(1); Annex VII; Recital 77

facts.statement: Manufacturer-built backends a product needs for a function are remote data processing and part of the product.
The Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026; software is a product and a vulnerability can be a defect.

National enforcement acts adopted by 30 Oct 2026: Finland (Act 439/2026), Hungary (Act CXXXV/2025), Malta (LN 238/2026); Germany's law passed the Bundestag plenary on 15 Oct 2026, promulgation pending. France has named ANSSI as notifying authority.
The Digital Omnibus COM(2025) 837 does not amend the CRA; Council mandate agreed 21 Oct 2026 (ST 14756/26); not adopted.
RED cybersecurity delegated act 2022/30 is repealed with effect from 11 Dec 2027 by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/339.
EUCC: 111 valid certificates from 9 certification bodies on 30 Oct 2026; the Art 27(9) act that would let EUCC replace third-party assessment is planned, not adopted.
Open-source stewards have a light-touch regime (Art 24) and are exempt from fines (Art 64(10)(b)); integrating FOSS never transfers the manufacturer's duty (Art 13(5)).
